I am an old man now, sixty years, and I have been farming these lands in the North West all my life. This beans plot is small, just over half a hectare, and I have intercropped it as we always do here in the Sudan Savanna — beans fix their own nitrogen so I do not waste my little fertilizer money on them, maybe just a small touch of NPK if I can afford it for the cereal mixed in. I will use my own seeds saved from last harvest like my father did, and rely on the rains since I have no fadama land. My sons and I will do most of the work ourselves, but during weeding and harvest I may call one or two neighbors to help for a few days.
